chunks: I ask Allah the Sublime to make for me an early relief from them, for by Allah, had it not been for my hope of meeting my enemy in martyrdom, and my preparing myself for death, I would have loved not to remain with these people for a single day, nor to meet them ever.
ai.seo_question: What motivated Imam Ali's patience with the people of Syria according to this supplication?
ai.summary: In this supplication from Nahj al-Balagha, Imam Ali (AS) articulates the psychological burden of political leadership amidst the Khawarij and Syrians, revealing that his endurance is sustained not by desire for power, but by the spiritual incentive of martyrdom (shahadah). This reflects the Shia scholarly understanding of his patience (sabr) as a conscious sacrifice for the preservation of the Ummah, distinguishing his rule from mere temporal governance. The reference to 'enemy' specifically targets the forces of Mu'awiya, highlighting the personal cost of his adherence to justice despite widespread opposition.
